questions.questionHtml:
Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?
15 + 5 × 8 – 72 ÷ 4 + 16 × 3 = 101
questions.solution:
Option 3) 5 and 3

After two numbers (not digits) interchanged then:

⇒ 15 + 3 × 8 – 72 ÷ 4 + 16 × 5 = 101 ⇒ 15 + 3 × 8 – 18 + 16 × 5 = 101 ⇒ 15 + 24 – 18 + 80 = 101 ⇒ 119 – 18 = 101 ⇒ 101 = 101

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow from the statements. Statements: All papers are pencils. All pencils are erasers. All erasers are pens. Conclusions: I. All pens are papers. II. Some papers are erasers. III. Some pens are pencils.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow from the statements.
Statements:
All papers are pencils.
All pencils are erasers.
All erasers are pens.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are papers.
II. Some papers are erasers.
III. Some pens are pencils.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:

Conclusions:

I. All pens are papers. - False (because All papers are pencils, All pencils are erasers and All erasers are pens. So, it can be possible but not definite)

II. Some papers are erasers. - True (because All papers are pencils, and All pencils are erasers. So, Some papers are erasers too)

III. Some pens are pencils. - True (because All papers are pencils, All erasers are pens, and All pencils are erasers. So, Some pens are pencils too)

questions.question: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 139 + 40 ÷ 5 − 168 × 3 = 283
questions.questionHtml:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
139 + 40 ÷ 5 − 168 × 3 = 283
questions.solution:
Option 3) ÷ and ×

Two signs need to be interchanged then:

⇒ 139 + 40 × 5 − 168 ÷ 3 = 283 ⇒ 139 + 40 × 5 − 56 = 283 ⇒ 139 + 200 − 56 = 283 ⇒ 339 − 56 = 283 ⇒ 283 = 283

questions.question: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P − M + R ÷ T × S’?
questions.questionHtml:
In a certain code language,
A + B means ‘A is the son of B’,
A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’,
A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and
A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’.
Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P − M + R ÷ T × S’?
questions.solution:
P is the wife of M, M is the son of R, R is the mother of T and T is the brother of S.

 

So, T is the 'Husband’s brother' of P.
